purpose: Conditionally selected design hypotheses that turn already-retrieved Knowledge into actionable exploration and checks. These are not peer-reviewed UI outcomes or universal prescriptions.
usage_policy: Require an actual query cue and a retrieved linked Knowledge card. Never show arbitrary advice, invent evidence, treat the link as proof, or force a visual style.

practices.name: Dense schedules and discoverable program information
practices.problem: People must find and compare a relevant item among a dense schedule without losing date, topic or speaker context.
practices.when: Many sessions or items span multiple dates and tracks, and users need targeted lookup rather than linear reading.
options: Group sessions by date or another task-relevant primary dimension, then offer a visible secondary filter.
Show the active filter state and count of visible matches; provide an obvious reset path.
Keep time, title, speaker and track scannable before expanding descriptions.
On narrow screens, prioritize task-relevant metadata rather than scaling a desktop grid.
failure_modes: Repeated cards that hide temporal relationships.
A filter with no active-state indicator or empty-results explanation.
Dense program information compressed into unreadable columns.
countercases: For five sessions on one day, a simple annotated list may be clearer than multi-step filters.
If speakers are intentionally unannounced, do not invent speaker identities.
checks: Find an AI session on a chosen date and return to all sessions.
Locate a session by speaker and identify the time.
At 320px confirm title, time and category remain distinguishable.
Using keyboard only, change and clear filters; confirm results update.

practices.name: Content relationships and information density
practices.problem: The layout hides semantic relationships behind repetitive containers, equal emphasis or arbitrary empty space.
practices.when: A screen presents heterogeneous content and its information hierarchy is unclear, especially across repeated sections.
options: List content roles and relationships before choosing a grid, table, timeline, comparison or narrative layout.
Create one dominant visual anchor and vary supporting element weight according to the task.
Group content through spacing and alignment before adding another border or card.
Compare at least one structurally different organization when the hierarchy remains ambiguous.
failure_modes: Using cards for every type of content without explaining why.
Equal-sized headings and sections that flatten priorities.
Removing so much decoration that the resulting page loses substance or useful emphasis.
countercases: Cards are effective when each item is an independently actionable peer.
A regular grid can be desirable for intentionally uniform catalogs.
checks: Ask a reviewer to name the primary action after a short glance.
Check headings and content relationships in a full-page screenshot.
Verify that each section communicates what the brief requires without dead space.
Check that a narrow viewport keeps the meaning rather than merely stacking boxes.

practices.name: Mobile composition and cross-viewport continuity
practices.problem: The mobile interface is only a squeezed desktop arrangement, weakening labels, content order, interaction or meaningful visual assets.
practices.when: The same content must work at 1440px, 390px and 320px, or long Korean content changes layout geometry.
options: Decide which content and actions must remain visible first on narrow screens.
Recompose navigation, comparisons and metadata presentation instead of only reducing font or column count.
Use alternative asset framing/cropping when the desktop picture becomes meaningless on mobile.
Test long headings, active filters, empty states and focus behavior at the narrowest width.
failure_modes: Unbounded horizontal overflow, clipped buttons or overlapped hero art.
Tiny labels preserved from a dense desktop dashboard.
Mobile-only omissions that remove essential task information.
countercases: Simple single-column content may adapt correctly with only fluid typography and spacing.
Do not invent a mobile-specific layout when the original already serves users well.
checks: Inspect first screen and full page at 1440, 390 and 320px.
Confirm interactive controls and error messages remain operable with a keyboard.
Compare visual priority of the same content across screen sizes.
Test a very long localized label and verify no text collision.

practices.name: Natural Korean UX writing and readable mixed typography
practices.problem: Mixed Korean/English content is unclear, unnaturally translated, crowded or truncated in real interface states.
practices.when: Text contains mixed scripts, variable Korean line length, honorific decisions, legal or precise product terminology.
options: Preserve meaning, action and actual product terms before improving sentence rhythm.
Check line breaks and truncation with the real copy rather than short placeholders.
Distinguish primary heading, actionable label, supporting text and metadata by role and scale.
Test form errors and confirmation messages for clarity and consistent Korean register.
failure_modes: A heading used as visual decoration rather than conveying meaning.
English literal translation that makes Korean error actions ambiguous.
Assuming W3C draft guidance experimentally proves a specific visual style.
countercases: Do not rewrite legally required or brand-approved terminology for elegance.
Multilingual UI may intentionally retain English product vocabulary.
checks: Read the actual Korean copy out loud and confirm the next action is clear.
Inspect 320px wraps, long Latin terms and mixed punctuation.
Test error, disabled and success states with localized content.
Check that the selected fonts cover characters used in the output.

practices.name: Form and choice-state feedback
practices.problem: A working component gives little feedback about its state, errors or keyboard path.
practices.when: Users must select, enter, correct or confirm something that has meaningful consequences.
options: Use explicit labels, validation errors close to the relevant control and a recoverable action.
Show selected filters or options, results counts and a clear reset path where appropriate.
Make modal focus entry, trapping, escape and restoration behavior predictable.
Distinguish loading, empty, error and success states with clear language.
failure_modes: Only color indicates a selected or failed state.
Errors appear after submission without location or recovery advice.
Modal appears visually but keyboard focus remains behind it.
countercases: Do not make trivial interactions artificially complex or add confirmations with no meaningful risk.
A static display without editing does not need a fake form.
checks: Complete the primary task with keyboard only.
Trigger and recover from an invalid input.
Open and close the modal, then confirm focus returns appropriately.
Change and clear a filter and observe both count and active state.

practices.name: Meaningful design directions before polish
practices.problem: Alternatives only change palette or surface effects while retaining the same information structure.
practices.when: A brief allows materially different user journeys or content relationships and early uncertainty is meaningful.
options: Write two distinct interpretations of the user goal before drawing detailed frames.
Compare content order, information relationships and effort, not just shades and card radii.
Select a direction using the task requirements; record why competing directions were rejected.
Prototype only when a static comparison cannot resolve an interaction uncertainty.
failure_modes: Three near-identical generic SaaS hero sections treated as different concepts.
Polishing the first idea before validating the core information path.
Producing options automatically for a trivial, already-settled request.
countercases: Simple maintenance fixes may not justify exploring multiple architectures.
Diversity without relevance can increase cost and reduce usability.
checks: Explain one structural difference between each option without mentioning colors.
Inspect whether authentic content still fits both options.
Compare paths for the user's primary task and one failure state.
Record decision rationale and unresolved uncertainty.

practices.name: Evidence-based rendered visual critique
practices.problem: Judging code or naming a defect without inspecting the actual rendered interface creates false confidence.
practices.when: A page exists and visual hierarchy, rhythm, overflow or responsiveness needs verification or revision.
options: Open captured pixels and prioritize issues by meaning, hierarchy, layout and task impact.
Record viewport and precise location for the observation; avoid unfounded aesthetic scores.
Make one meaningful revision before polishing colors, shadows or motion.
Capture the same viewport and state afterward, then describe observed differences.
failure_modes: Marking an issue fixed when the same screenshot was copied or renamed.
Replacing meaningful content with empty space while removing repeated patterns.
Equating an automatic screenshot check with WCAG certification or a user study.
countercases: If the issue is purely backend and has no rendered consequence, do not demand screenshot-based validation.
When the rendering environment is unavailable, report NOT EXECUTED rather than inventing observations.
checks: View the actual screenshot at the user-requested breakpoints.
Confirm first-screen purpose, main action, edge alignment and content continuity.
Verify the before/after files differ and describe what is visibly different.
Run task-specific functional and keyboard tests separately.
